title: Detection of muscle stem cell-derived myonuclei in murine overloaded muscles
protocol: Anesthetize adult mice by Isoflurane or anesthesia cocktail.
Shave the fur from the hind limbs using hair clippers.
Incise the skin on the hind limb to expose the gastrocnemius and soleus tendons.
Insert the tips of forceps into the underside of both tendons for cutting.
Cut through the gastrocnemius and soleus tendons precisely with micro-scissors.
Sanitize and wipe skin with 70% alcohol or related reagents.
Cut the skin to expose the plantaris and Achilles tendon.
Transect the distal Achilles tendons of both gastrocnemius and soleus muscles.
Remove 1 mm of the tendon to avoid reconnection during the experimental time course.
Suture the skin using surgical needle, suture, and a needle holder.
Dissect the plantaris muscle with sterile scissors and forceps.
Fix the dissected plantaris muscle for 2–5 min per muscle.
Optional: Isolate the jejunum and fix it using the same protocol as for muscle fixation.
If the target is a soluble factor, fix isolated plantaris muscle with 4% PFA for 30 min.
Replace sucrose in PBS (10% sucrose/PBS at 4°C for 3 h).
Replace with 20% sucrose/PBS at 4°C for 12–16 h.
Pick the distal tendon of isolated plantaris muscle using forceps and place it on kneaded tragacanth gum.
Soak the sample in cooled 2-methylbutane if it does not stand upright.
Freeze the plantaris muscle in liquid nitrogen-cooled 2-methylbutane for 1 minute with vigorous shaking using forceps.
Wait until the 2-methylbutane cools down completely and the white vapor disappears.
Immerse the muscle sample into the 2-methylbutane cooling with liquid nitrogen.
Remove 2-methylbutane from liquid nitrogen to allow the frozen 2-methylbutane to melt.
Place melted 2-methylbutane back into liquid nitrogen until the white vapor disappears again.
Immerse the muscle sample into the cooled 2-methylbutane.
Place the muscle samples on dry ice for 1 hour to vaporize the 2-methylbutane.
Store the muscle samples in closed containers at -80°C.
Take samples stocked in containers from the –80°C freezer and place in a cryostat.
Keep the samples in the cryostat for 10 minutes.
Make transverse cryosections (6 μm thick) on silane coated slide glass.
Transport stocked samples from the −80°C deep freezer on dry ice, not in liquid-nitrogen.
Cut off at least 1 mm of the proximal side of the plantaris muscle.
Cut non-sequential 10 cryosections per one muscle.
Place up to 40 cryosections on one slide.
Dry slides for 30 min at 15°C–25°C.
Trace around cryosections two or three times with a PAP pen (DAKO pen) to create a barrier.
Dry the barrier completely for 5 min at 15°C–25°C.
Cover the section with 4% PFA dissolved in PBS and incubate it for 10 min at 15°C–25°C.
Wash three times with 1× PBS containing 0.1% Triton X.
Treat the slides with 1× PBS containing 0.5% Triton X and incubate for 20 min at 15°C–25°C.
Wash thrice with 1 × PBS.
Prepare a reaction cocktail according to the Click-iT® EdU Imaging Kit instructions.
Cover sections with reaction cocktail (approximately 0.5 mL/slide).
Incubate for 30 min in the dark at 15°C–25°C.
Wash sections thrice with 80–100 mL 1× PBS containing 0.1% Triton X.
Cover sections with 5% skim milk dissolved in PBS (approximately 0.5 mL/slide).
Incubate for 1 h in the dark at 15°C–25°C.
Dilute primary antibody against dystrophin protein by 800 times with 5% skim milk in PBS (approximately 0.5 mL/slide).
Cover sections with diluted primary antibody and incubate overnight in humidified chamber in the dark at 4°C.
Wash sections thrice with 80–100 mL 1× PBS containing 0.1% Triton X.
Dilute secondary antibody by 500 times with 1× PBS (approximately 0.5 mL/slide).
Cover sections with diluted secondary antibody and incubate for 1 h in dark at 15°C–25°C.
Wash sections thrice with 80–100 mL 1× PBS containing 0.1% Triton X.
Adjust the exposure time and gain of each channel to blue (DAPI), green (dystrophin), and white (EdU).
Acquire individual blue, green, and white images in all areas of the plantaris muscle using All-in-one Fluorescence Microscope BZ-X700.
Use Keyence soft system (BZ-X Analyzer and Hybrid Cell count) or similar system to generate stitched images.
Count the number of EdU+ myonuclei located within myofibers marked by the dystrophin staining.
